content: Glorious and precious root guru,Please reside upon the lotus in my heart,Having cared for me through your great kindness,Please bestow the accomplishments of your body, speech, and mind.Glorious sole eye of all beings in the three realms,Unsurpassed protector of all who desire liberation,Possessing compassion greater than all the Victors,To the peerless, supreme guru, I pray.In the presence of the Victors, you took the vow of enlightenment,Renowned as Mañjuśrī in the abode of Tuṣita,In this Land of Snows, you are Losang Drakpa Pel;To you, the foremost heir of the Victors, I pray.Possessing the power of ripened, vast merit,You mastered the scriptures, Sanskrit grammar, and the like,And understood the sciences without having to study them;To you, whose qualities are spontaneously perfected, I pray.When you, the sun of your body, emerge from the cloud-bank of the Mother,You abandon forever the playful flickering of lightning,Which is the entanglement with the excellences of cyclic existence;To you, I pray.From your very youth, you were well-restrained by the supreme, blameless ethical discipline,Holding fast to the Victor’s entire ascetic path;In all your births, you possessed the power of being consistently vigilant;To you, I pray.With an analytical intellect that engages without obstructionIn the words and meanings of all the Victor’s scriptures,You zealously sought out excellent explanations;To you, the vast treasury of wisdom, I pray.You were never satisfied by mere strings of words,And regarding points difficult for millions of supreme scholars to fathom,With stainless, extremely subtle, and precise reasoning,You beheld all the teachings without exception; to you, I pray.Though all opponents trained in logicShould analyze your words a hundred times, O Protector,They remain free from shifting even slightly into any other form;To you who possess a pure mind, I pray.Who else but you beholds the scriptures as intendedBy the great pioneers of the Noble Land?To you, for whom all the scriptures arise as supreme instructions,I pray.Therefore, upon the crown of all supreme scholars,With lotus feet that always rest in peace,You are the dust upon which the ocean-clad earth is written;To you, who have become a stūpa for all beings, I pray.Though the Victors' wisdom may analyze it well,In your mind, the perfectly pure training of disciplineIs such that even the slightest fault of laxityIs nowhere to be seen; to you, I pray.Like a vast body of water, a source of precious jewels,How deep and vast is the compassion in your heart?It transcends the domain of all who possess the eye of primordial wisdom;To you, the venerable treasury of compassion, I pray.Without your altruistic intention,There would be no burden of benefit and happiness for embodied beings;You have reached the culmination of all vast conduct;To you, of wondrous courage, I pray.If even the mere breath from your mouth, O Protector,Becomes a cause of benefit for all beings,Then what need is there to mention your conduct of the two accumulations?To you, the friend of all beings in the three realms, I pray.Mañjughoṣa directly and perfectly instructs you,Day by day, with a stream of nectar—the eloquent teachings,The condensed essence of the wisdom-mind of the Victors of the three times;To you, who teach unceasingly, I pray.In this world, within the lotus grove of the Buddha’s teachings,You are like the sun of the Victors;Thus, the Protector Maitreya directlyPraised you as the supreme source of relief—to you I pray.You behold the victory banner of the bodies of countless Victors;Saraha, Luipa, and many otherGreat accomplished masters have directly blessed you;To you, the supreme and perfectly pure being, I pray.When the venerable Nāgārjuna, Āryadeva, Buddhapālita,And the feet of Candrakīrti blessed you,In that very instant, regarding the profound reality,You abandoned the stains of confusion—to you I pray.Because you have well-cultivated the supreme meditative equipoise,Which is like the center of the sky of reality,Your mind, even in the post-meditative state, is like an illusion,Unwavering for even an instant—to you I pray.The ultimate of all the Buddha's excellent explanations,The one who reveals the reality of the ocean of tantras,To you, inseparable from the Victorious All-Pervading Lord Vajradhara,The supreme Guru, I pray.Having seen exactly as they are the profound points of the two stages—The ultimate path never before experienced by others in this region—And having practiced that meaning,To you who have made this the essence of your practice, I pray.Having perfected the yoga of the coarse and subtle deities,You have cast far away all ordinary appearances, attachments, and conceptual thoughts;Because whatever arises is the manifestation of the mandala circle,To you whose mind is unwavering, I pray.The movement of conceptual winds has dissolved into the dhūtī,You behold the reality of the all-empty clear light;Possessing the manifestation of supreme great bliss in whatever arises,To you who possess the vajra mind, I pray.By the power of infinite prayers and skillful means,You effortlessly and spontaneously lead infinite hosts of disciplesOnto the path that delights the Victors;To you, the refuge of all the world, I pray.Through the asceticism of study and practice of the general teachings,At a time when the Buddha’s doctrine has been reduced to a mere name,You have made the Conqueror’s sublime Dharma—the scriptures and realizations of the three trainings—As bright as day; to you, I pray.When you, in accordance with your intention, were about to withdrawThe array of your physical manifestation from this realm,By the offerings of the hosts of daka heroes and dakinis,You filled the inconceivable sky; to you, I pray.Having manifested the clear light Dharmakāya,At that time your body became a mass of light;In the intermediate state, you attained the supreme siddhiOf the illusory body of complete enjoyment; to you, I pray.From this moment on, throughout all my lives,May I devotedly worship your lotus feet,And listening to your speech, please bless meTo accomplish only that which pleases you through all the activities of my three doors.Having abandoned the appearances of this life that seek gain and honor,And having abandoned the mind of peace that desires only one's own happiness,Please bless me so that I may never be separatedFrom the supreme bodhicitta that contemplates the benefit of beings.With subtle, wise, and precise intelligence,Following the reasoning of the Victor’s scriptures,Having mastered them entirely, please grant your blessingsTo dispel the great darkness of beings' ignorance.Having gained certainty in the meaning of the many tantra classes,And the profound meaning of the two stages, the ultimate excellent path,Without being swayed by any outer or inner adverse conditions,Please grant your blessings to practice them one-pointedly.In short, having well grasped the entirety of the Victor’s sacred Dharma,And in particular the unsurpassed Vajra Vehicle,Just as the Victorious One intended,Please grant your blessings to act as a guide for beings.Through this virtue, in all my lives,May I never be separated from you, the supreme guide and guru,And may I be sustained by the taste of the nectarExtracted from the heart-essence of your wisdom mind, O Protector.Furthermore, whatever virtuous actions I have performed,Or will perform in the future,May they all become the cause for you to joyfully take me under your care,And for me to practice solely in accordance with your commands.In all my lives, may the Victorious TsongkhapaAct directly as my spiritual friend of the supreme vehicle,And may I never turn away, even for a single moment,From that excellent path praised by the Victorious Ones.May I gain unerring certainty in the backbone of the Mahayana path—The bodhicitta, the key points of the authentic view, and the two stages—And through my diligence,May I make the practice of your teachings my core essence.Through the study and practice that views the three baskets and four classes of tantraAs the supreme instructions,May there be the auspicious glory of Blo-bzang-grags-pa,Who makes the Sage’s teachings flourish in all directions and at all times.This is a verse of supplication composed by way of briefly recounting the life story of the glorious, holy, and venerable great Jetsun Tsongkhapa, who is the embodiment of the wisdom and compassion of all the Victors condensed into one, and the crest jewel of all those of the five hundred [lineage]. It was requested with great insistence by many, beginning with the noble and disciplined monk Mchog-bzang-ba, and later repeatedly urged by the spiritual friend Nyi-ma-snying-po, who requested that I compose a supplication based on his life story that is easy to understand and not bound by the conventions of ornate poetry. Being also moved by my own supreme devotion, I, the learned monk Dge-legs-dpal-bzang-po—who lives by the grace of having been brought near to the lotus feet of that venerable Guru—have composed this. May it be auspicious in all directions and at all times.
